title: Global Inventory Synchronization for Retail Logistics
business: A regional retail chain expanding into national operations requires a centralized, consistent database for real-time inventory tracking across multiple warehouse locations.
problem: The current decentralized local database instances suffer from data drift and inconsistent stock levels, leading to frequent overselling and manual reconciliation overhead.
solution: Amazon RDS provides a managed relational database service that supports engines like PostgreSQL, allowing the retailer to centralize data in a single primary instance with automated backups and multi-AZ deployment for high availability.
steps: Provision an Amazon RDS instance using the PostgreSQL engine to serve as the single source of truth for inventory records.
Configure Multi-AZ deployment to ensure automatic failover and data redundancy across distinct physical locations.
Implement security groups to restrict database access strictly to the application tier VPC.
Enable automated backups with a defined retention period to facilitate point-in-time recovery.
Connect application services to the RDS endpoint to perform atomic inventory updates.
outcome: The retailer achieves a unified view of inventory across all regions, eliminating data drift and reducing the manual effort required for stock reconciliation.
limitation: A primary limitation is that Amazon RDS abstracts the underlying operating system, preventing direct root access to the database server; administrators can verify this by attempting to SSH into the instance, which will be rejected.

questions.question: In Global Inventory Synchronization for Retail Logistics, what is the primary problem addressed by Amazon RDS?
options: Data drift and inconsistent stock levels across decentralized databases.
High latency in global edge location content delivery.
Lack of container orchestration for microservices.
Inability to scale GraphQL API endpoints.
questions.explanation: The scenario explicitly identifies decentralized database drift as the core issue causing overselling.
questions.evidence: The current decentralized local database instances suffer from data drift and inconsistent stock levels, leading to frequent overselling and manual reconciliation overhead.

questions.question: In Global Inventory Synchronization for Retail Logistics, what is a specific limitation of using the managed service?
options: The inability to use PostgreSQL as a database engine.
The lack of automated backup capabilities.
The restriction on direct root access to the underlying operating system.
The requirement to manually manage physical hardware.
questions.explanation: Managed services abstract the OS, which prevents traditional root-level access.
